grammar_points.name: 〜ても (temo: even if)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add ても (temo) after the te-form of a verb to create a concessive — 'even if X happens'. The result doesn't change regardless of the condition.

Example from this song: 描いても (egaitemo) = 'even if I draw/imagine' — from 描く (egaku, 'to draw') → 描いて (egaite, te-form) + も (mo, 'even') = 描いても (egaitemo). Also: 掴んでも (tsukandemo) = 'even if I grab' and 躓いても (tsumazuitemo) = 'even if I stumble'

More examples:
• 食べる (taberu, 'to eat') → 食べても (tabetemo, 'even if I eat')
• 高い (takai, 'expensive') → 高くても (takakutemo, 'even if it's expensive')
• 雨 (ame, 'rain') → 雨でも (ame demo, 'even if it rains')

Note: For verbs, use te-form + も. For い-adjectives, change い to くても. For な-adjectives/nouns, use でも. ても shows resilience — the outcome stays the same no matter what.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 描く (egaku, 'to draw') → 描いて (egaite) + も (mo, 'even') → 描いても (egaitemo, 'even if I draw') / 掴む (tsukamu, 'to grab') → 掴んでも (tsukandemo, 'even if I grab')

grammar_points.name: 〜ていく (te iku: keep doing; gradually)

explanation.en:
How it works: Add ていく (te iku, literally 'do and go') after the te-form of a verb to express an action that continues moving away from the present state — 'keep doing' or 'gradually change'.

Example from this song: 遠ざかっていく (toozakatte iku) = 'keeps getting farther away' — from 遠ざかる (toozakaru, 'to move away') → 遠ざかって (toozakatte, te-form) + いく (iku, 'going')

More examples:
• 変わる (kawaru, 'to change') → 変わっていく (kawatte iku, 'keeps changing / gradually changes')
• 消える (kieru, 'to disappear') → 消えていく (kiete iku, 'fading away')
• 強くなる (tsuyoku naru, 'to become strong') → 強くなっていく (tsuyoku natte iku, 'keep getting stronger')

Note: ていく describes movement AWAY from now (into the future). Compare with てくる (te kuru), which describes movement TOWARD now (from the past). 寒くなっていく = 'it keeps getting colder' (future). 寒くなってきた = 'it has gotten cold' (until now).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 遠ざかる (toozakaru, 'to move away') → 遠ざかって (toozakatte, te-form) + いく (iku, 'go') → 遠ざかっていく (toozakatte iku, 'keeps getting farther away')

grammar_points.name: 〜続ける (tsuzukeru: keep doing)

explanation.en:
How it works: Attach 続ける (tsuzukeru, 'to continue') to the verb stem (masu-stem) to express doing something continuously over time — 'keep doing X'.

Example from this song: 探し続ける (sagashi tsuzukeru) = 'keep searching' — from 探す (sagasu, 'to search') → 探し (sagashi, stem) + 続ける (tsuzukeru, 'to continue')

More examples:
• 走る (hashiru, 'to run') → 走り続ける (hashiri tsuzukeru, 'keep running')
• 信じる (shinjiru, 'to believe') → 信じ続ける (shinji tsuzukeru, 'keep believing')
• 歩く (aruku, 'to walk') → 歩き続ける (aruki tsuzukeru, 'keep walking')

Note: The verb stem is the ます-form minus ます: 探します → 探し. 続ける itself can be conjugated: 探し続けた (kept searching), 探し続けている (has been searching).

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 探す (sagasu, 'to search') → 探し (sagashi, stem) + 続ける (tsuzukeru, 'to continue') → 探し続ける (sagashi tsuzukeru, 'keep searching')

grammar_points.name: 〜でしかない (de shika nai: can only be)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + でしかない (de shika nai) to express limitation — 'can only be X' or 'nothing more than X'. しか always pairs with a negative.

Example from this song: 僕でしかない (boku de shika nai) = 'can only be me / I'm nothing more than myself' — from 僕 (boku, 'I') + で (de) + しか (shika, 'only') + ない (nai, 'not')

More examples:
• 夢 (yume, 'dream') → 夢でしかない (yume de shika nai, 'it's nothing but a dream')
• 始まり (hajimari, 'beginning') → 始まりでしかない (hajimari de shika nai, 'it's only the beginning')
• 人間 (ningen, 'human') → 人間でしかない (ningen de shika nai, 'merely human')

Note: でしかない expresses humble limitation — accepting what you are or what something is. It can be self-deprecating or philosophical depending on context.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 僕 (boku, 'I') + で (de) + しか (shika, 'only') + ない (nai, 'not') → 僕でしかない (boku de shika nai, 'can only be me')

grammar_points.name: 〜であろうと (de arou to: whether...or)

explanation.en:
How it works: Use noun + であろうと (de arou to) to express 'whether it be X (or Y)'. It's a formal conditional showing indifference to conditions — the result holds regardless.

Example from this song: 架空であろうと現実だろうと (kakuu de arou to genjitsu darou to) = 'whether it be fiction or reality' — expressing that it doesn't matter which one it is.

More examples:
• 雨 (ame, 'rain') → 雨であろうと (ame de arou to, 'whether it be rain')
• 誰 (dare, 'who') → 誰であろうと (dare de arou to, 'whoever it may be')
• 何 (nani, 'what') → 何であろうと (nani de arou to, 'whatever it may be')

Note: であろうと is the formal equivalent of でも (demo). It's used in literary, poetic, or dramatic contexts. The pattern A であろうと B であろうと means 'whether A or B'.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 架空 (kakuu, 'fiction') + であろうと (de arou to, 'whether it be') + 現実 (genjitsu, 'reality') + だろうと (darou to, 'or') → 架空であろうと現実だろうと ('whether fiction or reality')

grammar_points.name: 〜なくても (nakutemo: even without)

explanation.en:
How it works: Take the negative form of a verb or adjective (ない), change to なくて (nakute), then add も (mo, 'even'). This means 'even without X' or 'even if there isn't X'.

Example from this song: 地図なんかなくても (chizu nanka nakutemo) = 'even without a map or anything' — from 地図 (chizu, 'map') + なんか (nanka, 'or anything') + なくても (nakutemo, 'even without')

More examples:
• お金 (okane, 'money') → お金がなくても (okane ga nakutemo, 'even without money')
• 分からない (wakaranai, 'don't understand') → 分からなくても (wakaranakutemo, 'even if you don't understand')
• 完璧 (kanpeki, 'perfect') → 完璧じゃなくても (kanpeki ja nakutemo, 'even if it's not perfect')

Note: なんか before なくても adds dismissive emphasis — 'something like a map' implies maps are unnecessary. The pattern is very empowering in this context.

grammar_points.conjugation_path: 地図 (chizu, 'map') + なんか (nanka, 'such a thing') + なくても (nakutemo, 'even without') → 地図なんかなくても (chizu nanka nakutemo, 'even without a map')
